key_insight: FiLIP trains CT representations around report-derived findings rather than treating different patients’ scans and reports as inherently dissimilar.
clinical_relevance: This approach could support CT finding classification and radiology report generation, though clinical utility is not established by the abstract.
method: Use a large language model to extract abnormal finding phrases from radiology reports.
Encode those findings with a biomedical text embedding model to construct target representations.
Train the CT image encoder to predict these finding-based representations.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports better multi-label zero-shot finding classification than weakly supervised approaches in in-domain and external-domain evaluations, plus benefits after fine-tuning for report generation.
watch_item: Reliance on automatically extracted findings may propagate report or extraction errors; the abstract provides no dataset sizes or numerical performance results.
paper_title: Findings-aware Language-Image Pretraining for CT Volume Interpretation
